edges.reason: Owned constructor assigns owner = msg.sender, making the caller the privileged owner.
acceptOwnership requires msg.sender == newOwner before transferring ownership.
transfer debits balances[msg.sender], so the caller controls the debited account.
approve writes allowed[msg.sender][spender] using the caller as the owner key.
transferFrom spends allowed[from][msg.sender] using the caller as the spender.
approveAndCall writes allowed[msg.sender][spender] and forwards msg.sender to the external receiveApproval call.
Constructor initialises the owner state variable from the untrusted caller.
transferOwnership, guarded by onlyOwner, writes the pending owner into newOwner.
acceptOwnership promotes newOwner into the owner state variable.
acceptOwnership clears newOwner to address(0) after the ownership handover.
onlyOwner modifier on transferOwnership compares msg.sender against the owner state variable.
onlyOwner modifier on transferAnyERC20Token compares msg.sender against the owner state variable.
transferAnyERC20Token directs swept tokens to the privileged owner address.
Token initialiser sets the symbol state variable.
Token initialiser sets the name state variable.
Token initialiser sets the decimals state variable.
Token initialiser sets the whole _totalSupply.
Token initialiser mints the entire supply into balances of a hard-coded address.
totalSupply() performs the unchecked subtraction _totalSupply - balances[address(0)].
_totalSupply is the left operand of the unchecked subtraction.
balances[address(0)] is the right operand of the unchecked subtraction.
balanceOf reads the balances mapping.
Caller-supplied tokenOwner selects the balance mapping slot.
transfer executes the balance mutation sequence.
transfer reads balances[msg.sender] and balances[to] before the safeSub/safeAdd computations.
transfer writes the safeSub/safeAdd results back into the balances mapping.
The 'to' parameter selects the credited balance slot in transfer.
The 'tokens' parameter is the amount transferred by transfer.
The caller-supplied amount feeds the safeSub/safeAdd balance arithmetic.
transfer invokes safeAdd for the recipient balance.
transfer invokes safeSub for the sender balance.
approve overwrites the allowed mapping entry without a double-spend check.
The spender parameter selects the allowance mapping key in approve.
The tokens parameter becomes the overwritten allowance value in approve.
transferFrom executes the balance and allowance mutation sequence.
transferFrom reads balances[from] and balances[to] for its safeSub/safeAdd computations.
transferFrom reads allowed[from][msg.sender] to decrement the allowance.
transferFrom writes the updated balances back into the balances mapping.
transferFrom writes the reduced allowance back into the allowed mapping.
The 'from' parameter selects the debited balance and the allowance owner.
The 'to' parameter selects the credited balance in transferFrom.
The 'tokens' parameter is the amount of the allowance and balance arithmetic.
transferFrom invokes safeAdd for the recipient balance.
transferFrom invokes safeSub for the sender balance and the allowance.
allowance reads the nested allowed mapping.
The tokenOwner parameter is the outer key of the allowance lookup.
The spender parameter is the inner key of the allowance lookup.
approveAndCall writes the allowed mapping before performing the untrusted external call.
approveAndCall always executes the external receiveApproval call on the attacker-chosen spender.
State (allowance) is already committed when control is handed to the untrusted spender contract.
The called spender contract can re-enter approveAndCall or transferFrom before the caller returns.
The spender parameter controls the allowance key written by approveAndCall.
The spender parameter is used directly as the callee address of the external receiveApproval call.
The tokens parameter is the granted allowance and is forwarded to receiveApproval.
The data parameter is arbitrary calldata passed through to receiveApproval.
transferAnyERC20Token performs an external transfer call to an owner-supplied contract.
The arbitrary token contract invoked by the privileged function can call back into this contract.
The tokenAddress parameter selects which contract is called.
The arbitrary tokenAddress becomes the callee of the external ERC20 transfer call.
The tokens parameter is the amount forwarded to the foreign token's transfer.
Parameter a is the first operand of safeAdd.
Parameter b is the second operand of safeAdd.
safeAdd computes the local result c = a + b.
Parameter a is the minuend of safeSub.
Parameter b is the subtrahend of safeSub.
safeSub computes the local result c = a - b.
Parameter a is the first factor of safeMul.
Parameter b is the second factor of safeMul.
safeMul computes the local result c = a * b.
Parameter a is the dividend of safeDiv.
Parameter b is the divisor checked by safeDiv.
safeDiv computes the local result c = a / b.
